summary: The core is one flat VHDL architecture split into char, background and sprite 'machines'. They all run off the raw hcnt/vcnt raster counters, fetch per pixel at scan time and keep raw PROM/RAM chip widths. The sprite path is built like hardware: a DMA counter fills four byte-lane sprite RAMs, a per-line adder/compare writes attribute words into a ping-pong 64x18 line buffer, and a loadable 4-bit counter strobes the shift registers that the graphics ROMs feed directly. Nothing is organized like MAME's draw_background/draw_sprites/tilemap. Against that, the protection device is a straight transliteration of MAME's protection_r/w, including the 'return 0' hack for E001. The scroll/palette registers are also latched on CPU writes rather than taken from the DMA'd buffer, so the lean is moderately toward hardware.

findings.signal: sprite engine as attribute line buffer + loadable start counter
findings.note: Sprite pixels come from a 4-bit counter sp_hcnt loaded with '01'/'11' & not hoffset depending on color. When it reaches F it reloads 16-bit shift registers that serialize ROM data at display time. MAME instead loops over attributes[64] and blits 16 pixels into a sprite bitmap.

findings.signal: per-line sprite Y adder/compare writing ping-pong line buffers
findings.note: sp_vcnt = vflip + ypos*2 - const, and a sprite is on the line when bits 8..4 are all ones. The match writes an 18-bit attribute word to one of two 64-entry buffers, selected by line parity and addressed by X[7:2], and the other buffer is read and cleared by hflip(8..3). This is an adder and buffer-swap structure, not C arithmetic.

findings.signal: sprite DMA via counter into four byte-lane RAMs
findings.note: One sp_ram_addr counter steps the work RAM at vblank. Its low two bits pick which of four 8-bit sprite RAMs is written, and on other lines the same counter reads them back in steps of 4. MAME just does a memcpy of dmasource into m_sprite_ram.

findings.signal: background X scroll as loaded counter, Y as per-line adder
findings.note: hshift is loaded with hoffset at hcnt=540 and then counts. vshift = voffset*2 + vflip + const is computed once per line, and nibble RAM data are selected by vshift(8) on hcnt phase. MAME computes roh = 0x38 + x/2 + scroll per pixel in a loop.

findings.signal: char layer as scan-time fetch, not tilemap
findings.note: The text and color RAMs are addressed directly by vflip(8..4)&hflip(8..4). Code and color are latched at hcnt(3..1)=111, and the graphics ROM bit is picked by hflip(3..1) every pixel. Bit 3 of color is duplicated onto the palette address like tied PROM pins.

findings.signal: raw PROM outputs as video DACs; sprite palette from two 4-bit PROMs
findings.note: The RGB lines are just the inverted PROM data bits. The sprite color is assembled from two separate 256x4 PROMs (rg/gb). MAME's res_net and pen-bank abstractions are absent.

Writing E001 shifts prot0<=prot1<=data, and reading E000 returns (prot1<<shift)|(prot0>>(8-shift)), the same as MAME's expression. E001 returns constant 00, which copies MAME's 'returning 0 seems to be enough' approximation instead of modelling the 7K/7J chip.

findings.signal: scroll/palette regs latched on CPU write, not from DMA buffer
findings.note: Writes to 8C00-8C03 are decoded directly into hoffset/voffset/palette registers instead of going through the DMA'd sprite buffer word 0. This is a register-level shortcut, closer to MAME's treatment of these bytes as named registers than to the board's data path.

findings.signal: ROM address/data descrambling identical to MAME bitswaps
findings.note: The address permutation with xor 0x03F/0x0FC and the data permutation 3,4,2,5,1,6,0,7 match MAME exactly. Any working core must reproduce this, and here it is done as wiring at runtime.

findings.signal: NMI enable from I register on refresh cycle; DSW mux via AY port B
findings.note: nmi_enable is taken from A8 during RFSH, and DSW2 bits are selected by IOB(3..1), the same as MAME. Both are required board behavior. The tpp2 watchdog that MAME models is missing.

findings.signal: ad-hoc fixes neither hardware nor MAME
findings.note: NMI is suppressed while the PC is between 3043 and 3046 for Sky Skipper, and the background is forced black when hoffset=0. These are empirical patches and do not come from either the board structure or MAME's code.
The per-pixel priority is bg < non-zero sprite < char, the same order as MAME's draw calls. A correct core must share this order, and here it is done per pixel.
